Arun (Eng): heads up — I converted from contractor -> full-time on 2026-05-20 but payroll still shows a 1099 for Jan-May. My year-to-date looks off and I need to file for a mortgage. How do we get W-2 wages reflected and/or correct the 1099?
Bea (People Ops): thanks Arun. Congrats on joining full-time! Did your conversion paperwork mark a retroactive hire date or was the employee start 5/20 only? Also did you submit I-9/W-4 on 5/20?
Arun (Eng): Employee start is 5/20. I signed W-4 + I-9 on 5/20 morning. But billing for Jan-May ran through vendor as contractor and I got paid via 1099 vendor code. I thought the conversion would trigger reclassification for the year but payroll said they'd still issue 1099 for contractor payments.
Sam (Payroll): quick context: contractor payments processed as vendor/1099 are separate from payroll W-2 wages. We can issue a W-2 for employee pay from 5/20 onward. For contractor income, if misclassification occurred (should've been employee earlier), we can escalate to request a reclassification and amended filings, but that is more involved. Did you perform employee-like work prior to 5/20?
Arun (Eng): yes, same duties, same schedule. The manager asked me to onboard as contractor quickly at the start of year due to headcount timing. We want to avoid mortgage issues — need proof of employment/income for Jan-May as W-2.
Marcus (Finance): lender requirements vary; many accept 1099 + recent W-2s but some want W-2 for full-year. If reclassification is appropriate, Payroll + Tax can assess. Two paths: 1) reclassify prior contractor pay to wages (requires vendor reversal + payroll reissue + amended 941/1099) or 2) provide a verification letter plus 1099s and current W-2 showing stable income. Which does Arun prefer?
Arun (Eng): I'd prefer reclassification if possible. Mortgage underwriter asked for year-to-date W-2 income. 1099 creates self-employed tax expectations and complicates debt ratios.
Alicia (Tax Counsel): high-level: reclassification is possible but depends on facts (behavioral, financial, relationship tests). Since Arun had employee-like integration, there's an argument. We'll need documentation: manager confirmation, original onboarding docs, timesheets, contract terms. If we proceed, steps: request vendor reversal, prepare payroll reissue for Jan-May, file amended payroll tax returns (941-X) and issue corrected 1099 (1099-CANCEL) or 1099 correction form. This usually takes 30-60 days and may require tax-advisor sign-off. There are potential liability implications; Finance should review.

Bea (People Ops): I've created ticket PO-2026-640 and uploaded initial docs. Arun please DM the onboarding chat and the contract you signed as contractor. Manager @Leah please confirm that Arun was performing staff-level duties Jan-May.
Arun (Eng): DMing contract and Slack threads now. Leah confirmed via DM.
Marcus (Finance): we'll model the employer-side liabilities and share a ballpark within 5 business days. If company accepts liability, we can proceed with reversals and amended filings. Otherwise we'll provide a verification letter for the lender.
Alicia (Tax Counsel): scheduling a call with our external payroll tax advisor to confirm reclassification mechanics and state-level impacts (TX->CA split because Arun did some CA work in April). State filings add complexity — TX has no income tax but CA employer obligations apply for CA-sourced wages. We'll include that in the call.
Sam (Payroll): note: this will likely generate amended 941s and potentially state equivalents plus corrected 1099. ETA 30-60 days after approval. We'll keep you posted in PO-2026-640.
Arun (Eng): thanks team. Appreciate the help — hope we can get this sorted quickly for the mortgage. :pray:
Bea (People Ops): we'll prioritize. Moving further docs into the private ticket. Keeping thread minimal. :white_check_mark:
